description: Send emails via SMTP. Works with Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, SendGrid, Mailgun, or any SMTP server.

attachments.description: File attachments as base64-encoded objects. Each item needs 'filename' (string) and 'data' (base64 string). Example: [{"filename": "report.pdf", "data": "base64data..."}]
attachments.title: Attachments

bcc.description: Blind carbon copy recipient(s). Separate multiple addresses with commas. BCC addresses are hidden from other recipients.
bcc.title: BCC

cc.description: Carbon copy recipient(s). Separate multiple addresses with commas.
cc.title: CC

html.description:
HTML email body. Takes priority over plain text in most email clients. Example: '

Hello

This is a test.

'
html.title: HTML Body

replyTo.description: Reply-to email address. When recipients reply, their response goes to this address instead of the sender.
replyTo.title: Reply-To

smtpHost.description: SMTP server hostname. Examples: smtp.gmail.com, smtp.office365.com, smtp.mail.yahoo.com, smtp.mailgun.org, smtp.sendgrid.net
smtpHost.sectionDescription: Provide your SMTP server credentials. For Gmail, use an App Password (not your regular password).
smtpHost.title: SMTP Host

smtpPassword.description: SMTP login password. For Gmail, use an App Password (Google Account > Security > App Passwords). For SendGrid/Mailgun, use your API key.
smtpPassword.title: SMTP Password

smtpPort.description: SMTP server port. Use 587 for STARTTLS (recommended), 465 for SSL/TLS, or 25 for unencrypted.
smtpPort.title: SMTP Port

smtpUser.description: SMTP login username. Usually your full email address. For SendGrid, use 'apikey' as the username.
smtpUser.title: SMTP Username

text.description: Plain text email body. At least one of 'Plain Text Body' or 'HTML Body' must be provided. If both are set, email clients choose which to display.
text.title: Plain Text Body

to.description: Recipient email address(es). Separate multiple addresses with commas. Example: 'user@example.com' or 'alice@example.com, bob@example.com'
to.title: To

useTls.description: Enable TLS encryption. Port 587 uses STARTTLS, port 465 uses direct SSL. Recommended: always keep enabled.
useTls.title: Use TLS/SSL

title: Send Email Input
